parts.title: Section 3
parts.passageHtml:
{[A.][296018]} {[600 years ago, roller coaster pioneers never would have imagined the advancements that have been made to create the roller coasters of today.][296019]} {[The tallest and fastest roller coaster in the world is the Kingda Ka, a coaster in New Jersey that launches its passengers from zero to 128 miles per hour in 3.][296043]} {[5 seconds.][296076]} {[It then heaves its riders skyward at a 90-degree angle (straight up) until it reaches a height of 456 feet, over one and a half football fields, above the ground, before dropping another 418 feet.][296079]} {[With that said, roller coasters are about more than just speed and height, they are about the creativity of the designers that build them, each coaster having its own unique way of producing intense thrills at a lesser risk than the average car ride.][296113]} {[Roller coasters have evolved drastically over the years, from their primitive beginnings as Russian ice slides, to the metal monsters of today.][296157]} {[Their combination of creativity and structural elements make them one of the purest forms of architecture.][296180]}

{[B.][296198]} {[At first glance, a roller coaster is something like a passenger train.][296200]} {[It consists of a series of connected cars that move on tracks.][296211]} {[But unlike a passenger train, a roller coaster has no engine or power source of its own.][296222]} {[For most of the ride, the train is moved by gravity and momentum.][296237]} {[To build up this momentum, you need to get the train to the top of the first hill or give it a powerful launch.][296251]} {[The traditional lifting mechanism is a long length of chain running up the hill under the track.][296274]} {[The chain is fastened in a loop, which is wound around a gear at the top of the hill and another one at the bottom of the hill.][296291]} {[The gear at the bottom of the hill is turned by a simple motor.][296318]} {[This turns the chain loop so that it continually moves up the hill like a long conveyer belt.][296332]} {[The coaster cars grip onto the chain with several chain dogs, sturdy hinged hooks.][296350]} {[When the train rolls to the bottom of the hill, the dogs catches onto the chain links.][296365]} {[Once the chain dog is hooked, the chain simply pulls the train to the top of the hill.][296383]} {[At the summit, the chain dog is released and the train starts its descent down the hill.][296402]}

{[C. Roller coasters have a long, fascinating history.][296421]} {[The direct ancestors of roller coasters were monumental ice slides – long, steep wooden slides covered in ice, some as high as 70 feet – that were popular in Russia in the 16th and 17th centuries.][296429]} {[Riders shot down the slope in sleds made out of wood or blocks of ice, crash-landing in a sand pile.][296464]} {[Coaster historians diverge on the exact evolution of these ice slides into actual rolling carts.][296482]} {[The most widespread account is that a few entrepreneurial Frenchmen imported the ice slide idea to France.][296498]} {[The warmer climate of France tended to melt the ice, so the French started building waxed slides instead, eventually adding wheels to the sleds.][296515]} {[ In 1817, the Russes a Belleville (Russian Mountains of Belleville) became the first roller coaster where the train was attached to the track (in this case, the train axle fit into a carved groove).][296540]} {[The French continued to expand on this idea, coming up with more complex track layouts, with multiple cars and all sorts of twists and turns.][296577]}

{[D. In comparison to the world’s first roller coaster, there is perhaps an even greater debate over what was America’s first true coaster.][296604]} {[Many will say that it is Pennsylvania’s own Maunch Chunk-Summit Hill and Switch Back Railroad.][296626]} {[The Maunch Chunk Summit Hill and Switch Back Railroad was originally America’s second railroad, and considered by many to be the greatest coaster of all time.][296642]} {[Located in the Lehigh valley, it was originally used to transport coal from the top of Mount Pisgah to the bottom of Mount Jefferson, until Josiah White, a mining entrepreneur, had the idea of turning it into a part-time thrill ride.][296669]} {[Because of its immediate popularity, it soon became strictly a passenger train.][296709]} {[A steam engine would haul passengers to the top of the mountain, before letting them coast back down, with speeds rumored to reach 100 miles per hour!][296721]} {[The reason that it was called a switch back railroad, a switch back track was located at the top – where the steam engine would let the riders coast back down.][296747]} {[This type of track featured a dead end where the steam engine would detach its cars, allowing riders to coast down backwards.][296776]} {[The railway went through a couple of minor track changes and name changes over the years, but managed to last from 1829 to 1937, over 100 years.][296798]}

{[E. The coaster craze in America was just starting to build.][296826]} {[The creation of the Switch Back Railway, by La Marcus Thompson, gave roller coasters national attention.][296837]} {[Originally built at New York’s Coney Island in 1884, Switch Back Railways began popping up all over the country.][296854]} {[The popularity of these rides may puzzle the modern-day thrill seeker, due to the mild ride they gave in comparison to the modern-day roller coaster.][296873]} {[Guests would pay a nickel to wait in line up to five hours just to go down a pair of side-by-side tracks with gradual hills that vehicles coasted down at a top speed around six miles per hour.][296901]} {[Regardless, Switchback Railways were very popular, and sparked many people, including Thompson, to design coasters that were bigger and better.][296937]}

{[F. The 1910s and 1920s were probably the best decade that the roller coaster has ever seen.][296959]} {[The new wave of technology, such as the “unstop wheels”, an arrangement that kept a coaster’s wheels to its tracks by resisted high gravitational forces, showed coasters a realm of possibilities that has never been seen before.][296976]} {[In 1919, North America alone had about 1,500 roller coasters, a number that was rising rampantly.][297012]} {[Then, the Great Depression gave a crushing blow to amusement parks all over America.][297028]} {[As bad as it was, amusement parks had an optimistic look on the future in the late 1930s.][297042]} {[But, in 1942 roller coasters could already feel the effects of World War Two, as they were forced into a shadow of neglect.][297060]} {[Most, nearly all of America’s roller coasters were shut down.][297083]} {[To this very day, the number of roller coaster in America is just a very tiny fraction of the amount of roller coasters in the 1920s.][297094]}

  2. There is a 3 both on the top and underneath the hill and it is powered by a 4 when it takes a turn.

questions.explanationHtml:
{[

chain

 

“Traditional roller coaster’s lifting force depends on a long time of _______ for climbing up,”: Lực nâng tàu lượn siêu tốc phụ thuộc vào … để đi lên.

 

Giải thích: Trong bài đề cập là cái “lifting mechanism” (cơ chế nâng của tàu lượn - tức là cách mà con tàu lên dốc) chính là sử dụng “a long length of CHAIN” (một sợi DÂY XÍCH - dây này đặt ở dưới đường ray - under the track).

][1]}

{[

loop

 

“..., which is connected firmly to a 28 _______ shape track.”: (dây xích) được gắn chặt vào một cái đường ray có hình dạng …

 

Giải thích: Tiếp theo câu trước, bài mô tả thêm là cái dây xích được “fastened” (thắt chặt) theo hình LOOP (hình VÒNG CUNG - bạn cứ hình dung là mình có một sợi dây xích, đem gắn 2 đầu lại với nhau, thì đó là một cái “loop”).

][2]}

{[

gear

 

“there are both 29 _______ on the top and underneath the hill…”: Đều có … ở trên và dưới dốc.

 

Giải thích: Người ta tiếp tục tả là cái vòng dây xích đấy được “wound around” (quấn quanh) một cái GEAR (bánh răng) ở “top of the hill” (trên dốc) và một cái nữa ở “bottom of the hill” (dưới dốc).

][3]}

{[

(simple) motor

 

“and it is powered by a _______ when it takes a turn.”: cái bánh răng này được vận hành bởi một cái … mỗi khi nó quay một vòng.

 

Giải thích: cái bánh răng được quay “by a SIMPLE MOTOR” (một cái động cơ đơn giản) → mọi người điền “simple motor” hoặc chỉ “motor” thôi cũng được nha.

The first roller coaster was perhaps originated from Russia which is wrapped up by 5, which was introduced into France, and it was modified to 6, because temperature there would 7 the ice. This time 8 were installed on the board.

In America, the first roller coaster was said to appear in Pennsylvania, it was actually a railroad which was designed to send 9 between two mountains. Josiah White turned it into a thrill ride, it was also called switch back track and a 10 there allowed riders to slide downward back again.

questions.explanationHtml:
{[

ice

 

“The first roller coaster was perhaps originated from Russia which is wrapped up by _______.” Cái tàu lượn siêu tốc đầu tiên có lẽ là bắt nguồn từ Nga và được phủ kín bởi … .

 

Giải thích: chỗ này giới thiệu về “direct ancestor of rollercoaster” (“tổ tiên” của tàu lượn siêu tốc - mình ngầm hiểu là những cái tàu lượn đầu tiên) là “long, steep wooden slides” (những cái cầu trượt dài bằng gỗ) và được “covered in ICE” (che phủ bởi BĂNG). ][5]}

{[

waxed slides

 

“which was introduced into France, and it was modified to 32 _______,”: từ Nga, cái phiên bản cầu trượt băng này được truyền sang Pháp và được biến đổi thành … .

 

Giải thích: Ý tưởng cầu trượt băng được “imported” (nhập khẩu) vào nước Pháp. Xong mình được biết thêm là do Pháo có “warmer climate” (khí hậu ấm hơn), người Pháp đã phải dựng WAXED SLIDES (CẦU TRƯỢT ĐƯỢC BÔI SÁP) thay vì cầu trượt băng.

][6]}

{[

melt

“because temperature there would … the ice.”: vì nhiệt độ ở đó (Pháp) có thể làm … băng.

 

Giải thích: ở câu trước đã nói rõ là Pháp có khí hậu ấm hơn (warmer climate) và điều này thường MELT the ice (làm TAN CHẢY băng)

][7]}

{[

wheels

 

“This time 34 _______were installed on the board.” Lần này thì … được gắn vào ván trượt

 

Giải thích: sau khi dùng cầu trượt sáp thì sau đó, người Pháp “adding WHEELS to the sleds” (gắn BÁNH XE vào xe trượt - tức là mấy cái cầu trượt này không phải là ngồi trượt xuống mà là có lót một cái ván cho người ta ngồi lên)

][8]}

{[

coal

 

“…it was actually a railroad which was designed to send _______ between two mountains.”: Cái tàu lượn siêu tốc đầu tiên ở Hoa Kỳ thực chất là một cái đường ray xe lửa dùng để gửi … qua lại giữa 2 ngọn núi.

 

Giải thích: cái đường ray ban đầu được dùng để “transport COAL” (vận chuyển THAN) từ đỉnh núi Pisgah tới chân núi Jefferson (tiếng Anh sẽ gọi núi bằng mount + tên núi)][9]}

{[

steam engine

 

“... a  ______ there allowed riders to slide downward back again.”: một cái … cho phép hành khách trượt xuống về chỗ cũ.

 

Giải thích: Một cái STEAM ENGINE (động cơ hơi nước) sẽ haul passengers (kéo du khách lên đỉnh núi) rồi cho họ coast back down (trượt xuống trở lại).

][10]}

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 11 - 14:

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 3?

In boxes 11-14 on your answer sheet, write:

YES                  if the statement is true

NO                   if the statement is false

NOT GIVEN    if the information is not given in the passage

questions.text: The most exciting roller coaster in the world is in New Jersey.
questions.explanationHtml:
NOT GIVEN

 

“The most exciting roller coaster in the world is in New Jersey.”: Cái tàu lượn siêu tốc kì thú nhất là ở New Jersey.

 

Giải thích: Trong bài chỉ đề cập là tallest và fastest → không khẳng định được là nó có “most exciting” hay không.

questions.text: French added more innovation on Russian ice slide including both cars and tracks.
questions.explanationHtml:
YES

 

“French added more innovation on Russian ice slide including both cars and tracks.”: Người Pháp cải tiến thêm cho cầu trượt băng của Nga, cả về xe trượt lẫn đường trượt.

 

Giải thích: Người Pháp đổi cầu trượt băng thành sáp (waxed slides) rồi thêm luôn bánh xe vào (adding wheels) cho xe trượt → có cải tiến, và cải tiến đủ cả 2 khía cạnh

questions.text: Switch Back Railways began to gain popularity since its first construction in New York.
questions.explanationHtml:
YES

 

“Switch Back Railways began to gain popularity since its first construction in New York.”: Đường tàu Switch Back bắt đầu trở nên phổ biến kể từ lần đầu tiên được dựng ở New York.

 

Giải thích: “originally built at New York’s Coney Island” (ban đầu được xây dựng ở khu vui chơi Coney Island ở New York), cái đường ray này bắt đầu “popping up all over the country” (nổi lên khắp nơi trong nước).

questions.text: The Great Depression affected amusement parks yet did not shake the significant role of US roller coasters in the world.
questions.explanationHtml:
NOT GIVEN

 

“The Great Depression affected amusement parks yet did not shake the significant role of US roller coasters in the world.” → Cuộc Đại Suy Thoái ảnh hưởng đến các công viên giải trí, nhưng không làm lay động vị thế của tàu lượn siêu tốc Mỹ trên thế giới.

 

Giải thích: Bài có đề cập đến việc các công viên giải trí bị ảnh hưởng bởi Đại Suy Thoái (gave a crushing blow to amusement) nhưng không nhắc gì đến vị thế của Mỹ → không khẳng định được thông tin “the significant role of US roller coasters”
